title: Discovery of Novel Inhibitors of a Critical Brain Enzyme Using a Homology Model and a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
summary: AtomNet, a deep convolutional network, helped identify five low-micromolar ANAT enzyme inhibitors using a homology model despite the lack of a native structure or high-identity template. This is biochemical hit identification for a Canavan-disease target, not evidence of treatment efficacy.
organization: Numerion Labs (United States); University of Toledo

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports five low-micromolar ANAT inhibitors. Indexed ACS text describes dose-response validation and comparison of AtomNet and smina rankings over a 7.2-million-compound library; full assay denominator and comparator details were not directly reviewed.
evidence.unknown: Full ACS Methods and supporting information were not reviewed. Exact assay denominator, comparator details, cellular target engagement, in-vivo efficacy and therapeutic safety were not assessed; biochemical inhibition does not establish treatment efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: AtomNet, a deep convolutional neural network, ranked candidate ligands for ANAT using a homology model and informed biochemical hit selection.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary PubMed abstract and publication metadata; full ACS Methods/supporting information not reviewed.
